projects.title: DailyDiff
projects.summary: Live LangGraph pipeline over 7 sources that emails a fact-checked brief 3× a week: 185 briefs, 42 editions.
projects.details: Autonomous multi-agent tech curation: a live LangGraph pipeline over 7 sources (including GitHub, Hacker News and Dev.to) that emails a fact-checked brief three times a week, 185 briefs across 42 editions so far. Cut LLM calls per run from up to 22 to 4 and added a fail-closed publish gate. Per-agent evals over 3 runs on 25 golden cases: the Skeptic rejected 6-7 of 7 noise items (3 of 7 before the fix), the Verifier caught 14-15 of 16 bad items, the Analyst matched 13-14 of 15 verdicts, and the Editor's 5 of 5 briefs passed structure checks. Stack: Python, LangGraph, LangChain, FastAPI, Mistral AI, Gemini, PostgreSQL (Neon), React, Vite, GitHub Actions, Brevo. Has a full case study on the site.
highlights: 7 sources incl. GitHub, Hacker News, Dev.to
LLM calls per run cut from 22 to 4

series.name: Not What You Think
series.about: Short posts on what people get wrong about LLMs, what is actually going on, and what it broke in my own builds.

posts.title: My prompt didn’t change. The model did.
posts.summary: A model my pipeline called disappeared from the API overnight. Pin model versions like you pin libraries, and test before you switch.

posts.title: The context window is a ceiling, not a target
posts.summary: A model with a 131,072-token window rejected my 10,411-token prompt: the rate limit hit first. Trimming, not a bigger model, fixed it.

posts.title: Temperature 0 makes answers less random, not fixed
posts.summary: Hosted APIs batch requests, so even temperature 0 can drift. Why my DailyDiff evals run three times and report ranges.

posts.title: AI reads tokens, not words
posts.summary: GPT-4o sees “strawberry” as three tokens, and one sentence costs 8 tokens in English but 27 in Hindi.
